question: Following the death of King Ahab, what geopolitical rebellion occurred, and what serious domestic accident incapacitated King Ahaziah in Samaria?

And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.\"

question: To which foreign deity did King Ahaziah dispatch messengers to inquire whether he would recover from his fall?

question: What stinging rhetorical question and fatal verdict did the angel of the LORD command Elijah the Tishbite to deliver to Ahaziah's messengers?
opt1: 'Why seek ye the living among the dead idols of Philistia? ... The kingdom shall be rent from thy hand and given to Hazael'
opt2: 'Have ye forgotten the fire on Mount Carmel and the slaughter at Kishon? ... Thy sickness shall consume thy flesh within seven days'
opt3: 'Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? ... Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die'
opt4: 'Will Baal heal the broken bones of the king of Samaria? ... Dogs shall eat the house of Ahab before the vintage of Jezreel'
correct: 'Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron? ... Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die'
explanation: Elijah intercepted the royal delegation with an indictment of Israel's functional atheism, declaring that Ahaziah's refusal to acknowledge God sealed his death sentence on his sickbed. 2 Kings 1:3-4 (KJV) - \"But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron? Now therefore thus saith the LORD, Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.\"

question: How did Elijah respond when the first captain of fifty marched up the hill with his detachment and commanded, 'Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down'?

explanation: When the royal officer treated the prophet as a mere civil subordinate, Elijah called down consuming supernatural fire, vindicating that the authority of God's word transcends all military coercion. 2 Kings 1:9-10 (KJV) - \"Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. explanation: Unwarned by his predecessor's destruction, the second captain arrogantly demanded Elijah come down 'quickly', only to be incinerated along with his fifty men by divine fire. 2 Kings 1:11-12 (KJV) - \"Again also he sent unto him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And Elijah answered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. opt1: The angel commanded Elijah to send a scroll of judgment to the palace while remaining safely atop the hill

question: What three geographic waypoints did Elijah and Elisha traverse before the Jordan crossing, and what solemn oath did Elisha repeatedly declare at each stop?

explanation: Retracing Israel's historical covenant path in reverse from Gilgal to Bethel, Jericho, and Jordan, Elisha demonstrated unflinching devotion, refusing three times to abandon his master. 2 Kings 2:1-6 (KJV) - \"And it came to pass, when the LORD would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, that Elijah went with Elisha from Gilgal. question: What tripartite military alliance marched through the wilderness of Edom to attack Moab, and what life-threatening crisis did they encounter after seven days?

question: How did King Jehoshaphat respond to Jehoram's despair, and how was Elisha identified by one of the king of Israel's servants?

explanation: While Jehoram blamed God for the crisis, godly Jehoshaphat sought divine counsel; Elisha was recognized by his humble past service as Elijah's personal attendant. 2 Kings 3:11 (KJV) - \"But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the LORD, that we may enquire of the LORD by him? And one of the king of Israel's servants answered and said, Here is Elisha the son of Shaphat, which poured water on the hands of Elijah.\"

question: With what scathing words did Elisha confront King Jehoram, and solely for whose sake did he agree to seek the LORD?
opt1: 'Why troublest thou the prophet of God? Go sacrifice to Baal-zebub... Had not Edom pledged loyalty, I would leave thee to perish'

opt3: 'What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother... Were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee'
opt4: 'Repent of the calves of Bethel before thou askest rain... Except for the sixty thousand warriors, thy bones would bleach in Edom'
correct: 'What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother... Were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee'
explanation: Elisha bluntly told apostate Jehoram to consult the pagan court prophets of Ahab and Jezebel, declaring that only respect for righteous Jehoshaphat restrained him from turning his back. 2 Kings 3:13-14 (KJV) - \"And Elisha said unto the king of Israel, What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother. And the king of Israel said unto him, Nay: for the LORD hath called these three kings together, to deliver them into the hand of Moab. And Elisha said, As the LORD of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward thee, nor see thee.\"

question: What unusual medium did Elisha request to prepare his spirit for prophecy, and what miraculous instruction followed?

opt3: He requested forty priests to blow silver trumpets; as they sounded, he prophesied a flood from the hills

correct: He called for a minstrel; as the minstrel played, the hand of the LORD came upon him, and he said: 'Make this valley full of ditches'
explanation: Sacred music calmed and focused the prophet's spirit; under divine inspiration, Elisha commanded the parched valley to be dug full of catchment ditches in anticipation of unseen water. 2 Kings 3:15-16 (KJV) - \"But now bring me a minstrel. And it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him. And he said, Thus saith the LORD, Make this valley full of ditches.\"

question: What remarkable atmospheric conditions accompanied the filling of the valley with water?
opt1: 'Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye, and your cattle, and your beasts'

correct: 'Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye, and your cattle, and your beasts'
explanation: Without a single gust of local wind or cloud of local rain, flash floods from a distant cloudburst in the Edomite mountains rushed into the valley, filling every trench overnight. 2 Kings 3:17 (KJV) - \"For thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, that ye may drink, both ye, and your cattle, and your beasts.\"

question: At what specific liturgical time did the water arrive, and what visual illusion lured the Moabite army into a fatal trap?

opt4: At high noon; a mirage on the salt plains made the trenches look like a vast ditch of abandoned plunder

explanation: Arriving precisely at the hour of the morning temple sacrifice in Jerusalem, the water reflected the morning sun over Edom's red earth; deceived into thinking the allies had massacred each other, Moab rushed in disorganized for spoil. 2 Kings 3:20-23 (KJV) - \"And it came to pass in the morning, when the meat offering was offered, that, behold, there came water by the way of Edom, and the country was filled with water. And when all the Moabites heard that the kings were come up to fight against them, they gathered all that were able to put on armour, and upward, and stood in the border. And they rose up early in the morning, and the sun shone upon the water, and the Moabites saw the water on the other side as red as blood: And they said, This is blood: the kings are surely slain, and they have smitten one another: now therefore, Moab, to the spoil.\"

question: How did the allied forces devastate the territory of Moab according to the prophetic directive?
opt1: They burned all forty walled fortresses with sulfur, salted the vineyards of Ar, and banished fifty thousand captives

explanation: The allied armies executed total scorched-earth retribution across Moab, filling fertile fields with stones, blocking life-giving springs, and cutting down all fruit-bearing trees. 2 Kings 3:24-25 (KJV) - \"And when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and smote the Moabites, so that they fled before them: but they went forward smiting the Moabites, even in their country. And they beat down the cities, and on every good piece of land cast every man his stone, and filled it; and they stopped all the wells of water, and felled all the good trees: only in Kirharaseth left they the stones thereof; howbeit the slingers went about it, and smote it.\"

question: What horrific desperate act did Mesha king of Moab commit upon the wall of Kir-haraseth when his breakout assault failed?

Then he took his eldest son that should have reigned in his stead, and offered him for a burnt offering upon the wall. And there was great indignation against Israel: and they departed from him, and returned to their own land.\"

question: What desperate domestic crisis prompted the widow of one of the sons of the prophets to cry out to Elisha?
opt1: Her ancestral land in Jericho had been confiscated by the tax collectors of King Jehoram
opt2: A severe famine had left her household with only bitter herbs, and her elderly mother was near death

explanation: Under ancient insolvency laws, an unpaid creditor could seize a debtor's children as bondservants; the destitute widow of a faithful prophet appealed to Elisha for divine intervention. 2 Kings 4:1 (KJV) - \"Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the LORD: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen.\"

question: What single item remained in the widow's house, and what specific instructions did Elisha give her?
opt1: A pot of oil; he instructed her to borrow empty vessels of all her neighbours, not a few, shut the door upon herself and sons, and pour out into all those vessels

opt4: A small cruse of honey; he directed her to pour it upon the threshold and pray until sunrise
correct: A pot of oil; he instructed her to borrow empty vessels of all her neighbours, not a few, shut the door upon herself and sons, and pour out into all those vessels
explanation: God works through what little is consecrated to Him: with only a single flask of olive oil, the widow demonstrated faith by gathering empty jars from all her neighbors to receive the miraculous overflow. 2 Kings 4:2-4 (KJV) - \"And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil. Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few. And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.\"

question: When did the miraculous multiplication of oil cease, and what final counsel did the man of God provide?
opt1: The oil ceased at the seventh jar; Elisha told her to give half to the school of prophets and bury the rest

explanation: The divine supply was limited only by human vessel capacity; the oil flowed until every jar was filled, providing more than enough capital to extinguish the debt and provide perpetual livelihood. 2 Kings 4:6-7 (KJV) - \"And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed. Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.\"

question: How did the wealthy woman of Shunem demonstrate extraordinary hospitality to Elisha as he passed through her city?

opt4: She prepared an annual banquet for fifty sons of the prophets and clothed Elisha in fine linen vestments
correct: She constrained him to eat bread, and persuaded her husband to make a little chamber on the wall furnished with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick
explanation: Discerning Elisha as a holy man of God, the noble Shunammite woman created a tranquil, dedicated prophet's chamber with four essential amenities: bed, table, chair, and lampstand. 2 Kings 4:8-10 (KJV) - \"And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread. And so it was, that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread. And she said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually. Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.\"

question: What miraculous reward did Elisha promise the Shunammite woman after Gehazi noted her childlessness and elderly husband?
opt1: 'Thy storehouses shall never lack wheat and wine for seven generations'
opt2: 'The king of Israel shall grant thy husband hereditary tax exemption in Jezreel'
opt3: 'Thou shalt be remembered as a mother in Israel, and two daughters shall be born to thee'
opt4: 'About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son'

explanation: Though the woman had asked for nothing, God honored her selfless hospitality by reversing her husband's barren line, promising a son within a year despite her initial disbelief. 2 Kings 4:14-16 (KJV) - \"And he said, What then is to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old. And he said, Call her. And when he had called her, she stood in the door. And he said, About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.\"

question: What tragedy struck the child as he grew, and what did the Shunammite mother immediately do?
opt1: He cried 'My head, my head' in the harvest field and died on her knees at noon; she laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door, and set out for Mount Carmel

explanation: Suffering likely sunstroke in the harvest fields, the boy died on his mother's lap; demonstrating magnificent faith, she placed his body on Elisha's bed, sealed the room, and galloped straight to Carmel. 2 Kings 4:18-22 (KJV) - \"And when the child was grown, it fell on a day, that he went out to his father to the reapers. And he said unto his father, My head, my head. And he said to a lad, Carry him to his mother. And when he had taken him, and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees till noon, and then died. And she went up, and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door upon him, and went out. And she called unto her husband, and said, Send me, I pray thee, one of the young men, and one of the asses, that I may run to the man of God, and come again.\"

question: What answer did the Shunammite woman give when Gehazi inquired whether it was well with her, her husband, and the child?
opt1: She cried, 'Death hath entered my home, and the boy is no more'
opt2: She answered, 'It is well'
opt3: She answered, 'The hand of the LORD is heavy upon Shunem'
opt4: She whispered, 'Trouble not the prophet, for my soul is broken'

explanation: Her famous declaration 'It is well' (Shalom) was an expression of transcendent covenant faith, refusing to unveil her crisis to the servant until she could grasp the feet of the man of God himself. 2 Kings 4:25-26 (KJV) - \"So she went and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her afar off, that he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, yonder is that Shunammite: Run now, I pray thee, to meet her, and say unto her, Is it well with thee? is it well with thy husband? is it well with the child? And she answered, It is well.\"

question: What physical actions did Elisha perform in the upper chamber to resurrect the Shunammite's son?

opt4: He prayed facing Jerusalem, touched the boy's chest with Elijah's mantle, and shouted with a loud voice

explanation: Through prolonged, physically intimate intercession and intense prayer, God channeled life back into the boy; seven sneezes signaled the clearing of his respiratory tract as full vitality returned. 2 Kings 4:33-35 (KJV) - \"He went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the LORD. And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands: and he stretched himself upon the child; and the flesh of the child waxed warm. Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.\"

question: How did Elisha neutralize the poisonous stew during a time of dearth at Gilgal when wild gourds were mistakenly shredded into the pot?

opt2: He cast salt and wild honey into the boiling kettle, neutralizing the venomous herb immediately

opt4: When they cried 'O thou man of God, there is death in the pot', Elisha cast meal into the pot, saying: 'Pour out for the people, that they may eat'; and there was no harm in the pot

explanation: When bitter, toxic wild gourds (colocynths) contaminated the communal pot, Elisha introduced ordinary grain meal—a symbol of life and covenant offering—miraculously rendering the food wholesome. 2 Kings 4:38-41 (KJV) - \"And Elisha came again to Gilgal: and there was a dearth in the land; and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him: and he said unto his servant, Set on the great pot, and seethe pottage for the sons of the prophets. And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourds his lap full, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew them not. So they poured out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the pottage, that they cried out, and said, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot. And they could not eat thereof. But he said, Then bring meal. And he cast it into the pot; and he said, Pour out for the people, that they may eat. And there was no harm in the pot.\"

question: What miracle of multiplication did Elisha perform when a man from Baal-shalisha brought twenty loaves of barley and full ears of corn in the husk?

And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat. And his servitor said, What, should I set this before an hundred men? He said again, Give the people, that they may eat: for thus saith the LORD, They shall eat, and shall leave thereof. So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD.\"

question: How does 2 Kings 5 describe Naaman's high military status in Syria alongside his tragic personal affliction?

explanation: Scripture explicitly credits Yahweh with using Naaman to give military victory to Syria; yet despite all his royal honors, bravery, and triumphs, the devastating clause stood: 'he was a leper'. 2 Kings 5:1 (KJV) - \"Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.\"

question: Through whose humble testimony was Naaman first directed toward the healing power of the God of Israel?
opt1: An Israelite merchant captured in the skirmishes of Gilead who traded fine linen in Damascus
opt2: A little captive maid from the land of Israel, who waited on Naaman's wife, saying: 'Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy'

opt4: A traveling Phoenician physician who had heard of the miracles performed by the prophet of Samaria
correct: A little captive maid from the land of Israel, who waited on Naaman's wife, saying: 'Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy'
explanation: In a magnificent display of divine providence, God used an unnamed, enslaved young Hebrew girl—holding no bitterness toward her captors—to point the supreme general of Syria to the true prophet. 2 Kings 5:2-3 (KJV) - \"And the Syrians had gone out by companies, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid; and she waited on Naaman's wife. And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.\"

question: What lavish gifts did Naaman take with him to Israel, and why did the king of Israel rend his clothes upon reading the Syrian king's letter?

opt4: Twenty talents of refined copper and royal cedar timber; the king tore his robes because leprosy was defiling his court

explanation: Naaman brought enormous wealth equivalent to millions of dollars; but King Jehoram, spiritually blind and faithless, panicked, interpreting the request to heal leprosy as an impossible diplomatic trap to justify invasion. 2 Kings 5:5-7 (KJV) - \"And the king of Syria said, Go to, go, and I will send a letter unto the king of Israel. And he departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment. And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter is come unto thee, behold, I have therewith sent Naaman my servant to thee, that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy. And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.\"

question: What message did Elisha send to the distressed king of Israel upon hearing that the monarch had rent his clothes?
opt1: 'Fear not the king of Syria, for his army shall be consumed like grass before the Jordan'
opt2: 'Send the Syrian captain to the waters of Siloam, that the glory of Jerusalem may be revealed'

opt4: 'Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel'

explanation: Elisha intervened to vindicate God's honor before the nations, rebuking the king's faithless despair and declaring that the Syrian general would discover that the living God has a true prophet in Israel. 2 Kings 5:8 (KJV) - \"And it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.\"

question: What humble, unexpected prescription did Elisha deliver through a messenger to Naaman waiting at his door?
opt1: 'Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean'

opt4: 'Fast for seven days in sackcloth outside the gates, and call upon the God of Abraham at sunrise'

explanation: Elisha did not even emerge from his house, refusing to flatter the general's pride; he sent a simple instruction to dip seven times in the muddy Jordan River, demanding absolute humility and faith. 2 Kings 5:9-10 (KJV) - \"So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha. And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.\"

question: Why did Naaman turn away in rage, and which famous rivers of Damascus did he compare favorably to the waters of Israel?

opt4: He feared contracting river fever; complaining: 'The sparkling waters of Hamath surpass all the muddy brooks of Ephraim'
correct: He expected the prophet to come out, stand, call on God, and strike his hand over the place; exclaiming: 'Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?'
explanation: Naaman's aristocratic pride was deeply offended by Elisha's refusal to perform a dramatic, theatrical healing ritual; he indignantly exalted the crystalline mountain rivers of Damascus over the muddy Jordan. 2 Kings 5:11-12 (KJV) - \"But Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper. Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.\"

question: With what wise, respectful logic did Naaman's servants persuade their master to obey Elisha's directive?

question: In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, what administrative mission did he dispatch Shaphan the scribe to execute in the temple?

explanation: Zedekiah's political blindness was judicial hardening: God in His holy wrath gave the apostate leadership over to their own foolish counsel, executing the final decree of expulsion from His presence. 2 Kings 24:20 (KJV) - \"For through the anger of the LORD it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.\"

question: Who was the queen mother of King Jehoiachin who was deported with him into Babylonian exile?
opt1: Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem
opt2: Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah
opt3: Zibiah, of Beer-sheba
opt4: Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath
correct: Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem
explanation: Nehushta, the influential queen mother, accompanied her young son into exile, fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy that the crown would be cast down and the queen mother exiled (Jeremiah 13:18; 22:26). 2 Kings 24:8-12 (KJV) - \"Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. And his mother's name was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem. And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done. At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged. And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, and his servants did besiege it. And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his officers: and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.\"

question: On what exact date did Nebuchadnezzar launch the final siege of Jerusalem, and how long did the city hold out?
opt1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month; and the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of King Zedekiah (about eighteen months)
opt2: In the seventh year, on the first day of the seventh month; holding out for three full years
opt3: In the fifth year, on the fifteenth day of the first month; holding out for seven months
opt4: In the tenth year, on the fourth day of the fifth month; holding out for twelve months
correct: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month; and the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of King Zedekiah (about eighteen months)
explanation: The final death-siege of Jerusalem began on the 10th of Tevet in 588 BC (commemorated in the Jewish calendar), lasting an agonizing eighteen months until starvation broke all defense. 2 Kings 25:1-2 (KJV) - \"And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about. And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.\"

question: What internal horror broke the resistance of Jerusalem on the ninth day of the fourth month in the eleventh year of Zedekiah?
opt1: A massive earthquake shattered the eastern wall and crushed the royal garrison
opt2: The famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land; and the city was broken up
opt3: Babylonian fire arrows burned the temple roof and ignited thirty grain storehouses
opt4: A sudden plague of pestilence struck seventy thousand citizens dead in three days
correct: The famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land; and the city was broken up
explanation: By July 586 BC (9th of Tammuz), food was completely exhausted; with defenders too weak from starvation to hold their weapons, the Babylonian siege engines breached the city walls. 2 Kings 25:3-4 (KJV) - \"And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land. And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king's garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain.\"

question: What gruesome judgment was executed upon King Zedekiah at Riblah after he was captured in the plains of Jericho?
opt1: They hanged Zedekiah from a tree fifty cubits high in the sight of all the Chaldean captains
opt2: They drowned Zedekiah in the river Orontes and cast his sons into the furnace of Babylon
opt3: They slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon
opt4: They stripped off his royal robes and forced him to pull Nebuchadnezzar's chariot barefoot to Nineveh
correct: They slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon
explanation: Zedekiah suffered a horrific fate: the last sight he ever saw was the slaughter of his royal sons before his eyes were gouged out, fulfilling both Jeremiah 34:3 and Ezekiel 12:13 (he went to Babylon, but never saw it). 2 Kings 25:6-7 (KJV) - \"So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him. And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.\"

question: What total destruction did Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, inflict on Jerusalem in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar (586 BC)?
opt1: He dismantled the palace of Solomon, but preserved the Holy of Holies as a sanctuary for Babylonian gods
opt2: He burned the outer suburbs and tore down forty cubits of the western wall, sparing the temple
opt3: He spared the great houses of the nobles, but leveled the foundations of the citadel of Millo
opt4: He burnt the house of the LORD, the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; and the army of the Chaldees brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about
correct: He burnt the house of the LORD, the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; and the army of the Chaldees brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about
explanation: On the 9th of Av (Tisha B'Av) in 586 BC, Nebuzaradan executed total incineration: Solomon's magnificent temple, the royal palace complex, and every prominent building were burned to ash, and the walls razed. 2 Kings 25:8-10 (KJV) - \"And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem: And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man's house burnt he with fire. And all the army of the Chaldees, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.\"

question: What happened to Solomon's monumental bronze architectural masterpieces—the two pillars (Jachin and Boaz) and the Molten Sea?
opt1: The pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the LORD, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon
opt2: They were rolled intact onto cedar wagons and dedicated in the temple of Marduk in Babylon
opt3: They were melted on site in the valley of Hinnom to forge fifty iron battering rams
opt4: They were thrown into the Dead Sea to prevent them from being defiled by foreign conquerors
correct: The pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the LORD, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon
explanation: Too immense to transport whole, Hiram's eighteen-cubit bronze pillars (Jachin and Boaz), the wheeled bases, and the massive Molten Sea were smashed into fragments and carted to Babylon as scrap metal. 2 Kings 25:13 (KJV) - \"And the pillars of brass that were in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the LORD, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.\"

question: What prominent religious and civil leaders were captured in Jerusalem and executed by Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah?
opt1: The prophet Jeremiah, forty levitical singers, and twenty elders of the tribe of Benjamin
opt2: Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, three keepers of the door, the military muster officer, five men of the king's presence, the chief scribe, and sixty men of the people
opt3: The sons of Jehoiada, thirty royal cupbearers, and the master of the palace armory
opt4: The seventy judges of the Sanhedrin and fifty craftsmen of the goldsmith guild
correct: Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, three keepers of the door, the military muster officer, five men of the king's presence, the chief scribe, and sixty men of the people
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar systematically liquidated the remaining leadership of the theocracy: high priest Seraiah (grandfather of Ezra), second priest Zephaniah, cabinet ministers, and sixty prominent citizens were executed at Riblah. 2 Kings 25:18-21 (KJV) - \"And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door: And out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war, and five men of them that were in the king's presence, which were found in the city, and the principal scribe of the host, which mustered the people of the land, and threescore men of the people of the land that were found in the city: And Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took these, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah: And the king of Babylon smote them, and slew them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away out of their land.\"

question: Whom did the king of Babylon appoint as governor over the impoverished remnant left in the land of Judah?
opt1: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the seed royal
opt2: Johanan the son of Kareah, captain of the forces
opt3: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan
opt4: Baruch the son of Neriah, the scribe of Jeremiah
correct: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan
explanation: Nebuchadnezzar established a provincial capital at Mizpah under Gedaliah, a member of the noble, godly scribal family of Shaphan that had long supported Jeremiah and supported submission to Babylon. 2 Kings 25:22 (KJV) - \"And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler.\"

question: What treacherous act assassinated Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah, and what panic-stricken migration followed?
opt1: A Syrian raiding party ambushed Gedaliah; and the remaining citizens fled into the mountains of Moab
opt2: Edomite bandits poisoned the cistern of Mizpah; and the remnant escaped to the seaport of Tyre
opt3: Babylonian garrison soldiers mutinied; and the Jewish survivors fled across the Euphrates
opt4: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the seed royal, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah that he died; and all the people, small and great, and the captains, arose and came to Egypt for fear of the Chaldees
correct: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the seed royal, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah that he died; and all the people, small and great, and the captains, arose and came to Egypt for fear of the Chaldees
explanation: Ishmael, a fanatical Davidic royalist backed by Ammon, assassinated Gedaliah; terrified of Babylonian collective reprisal, the surviving Jewish remnant fled to Egypt, taking Jeremiah with them. 2 Kings 25:25-26 (KJV) - \"But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah. And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees.\"

question: What unexpected reversal of fortune favored exiled King Jehoiachin in Babylon thirty-seven years into his captivity?
opt1: Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he began to reign, did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison, spoke kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon
opt2: Nebuchadnezzar pardoned Jehoiachin on his deathbed and sent him back to rebuild Jerusalem
opt3: Cyrus king of Persia conquered Babylon and crowned Jehoiachin governor of Judea
opt4: Darius the Mede released Jehoiachin and restored seventy golden vessels to his hand
correct: Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he began to reign, did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison, spoke kindly unto him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon
explanation: In 561 BC, Nebuchadnezzar's successor Evil-merodach (Amel-Marduk) pardoned Jehoiachin after 37 years in a dungeon, exalting him above all other captive kings in Babylon. 2 Kings 25:27-28 (KJV) - \"And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon;\"

question: With what tender, hopeful note of divine covenant preservation does the book of 2 Kings conclude?
opt1: The temple was rebuilt in Jerusalem forty years after the departure of the glory
opt2: Jehoiachin changed his prison garments, did eat bread continually before the king all the days of his life, and received a continual allowance every day a portion until the day of his death
opt3: The walls of Zion were restored by thirty thousand returning exiles from the Euphrates
opt4: The Ark of the Covenant was discovered intact in the secret chambers of Mount Horeb
correct: Jehoiachin changed his prison garments, did eat bread continually before the king all the days of his life, and received a continual allowance every day a portion until the day of his death
explanation: The book of 2 Kings ends on a shining beam of messianic hope: the Davidic heir is preserved alive, elevated in honor, and sustained with royal daily bread—signaling that God's eternal covenant with David remains unbroken. 2 Kings 25:29-30 (KJV) - \"And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life.\"
